job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

response.passage: On 14th August, our science teacher, Mr. Sharma, conducted an experiment in the school laboratory to demonstrate how current flows through a circuit. He placed a small copper wire, a battery, and a glowing bulb on the wooden table. Rohan, who was sitting near the window, observed that the bulb lit up immediately when the switch was closed. Mr. Sharma explained that the movement of electrons through the wire causes the bulb to glow. To test our understanding, he asked us to replace the copper wire with a piece of dry string. We noticed that the bulb remained dark because the string does not allow electricity to pass through it. Later, Priya noted that the battery felt warm after 10 minutes of continuous use. Mr. Sharma clarified that the internal resistance of the battery generates heat as a result of the current flow. We learned that while metals like copper are excellent conductors, materials like string act as insulators. The experiment concluded at 11:30 AM, leaving us with a clear idea of how components interact in a simple loop.
response.summary: Mr. Sharma demonstrated an electrical circuit experiment using a battery, bulb, and different materials. The class observed how conductors allow current to flow while insulators block it. They also learned that current flow can cause battery components to heat up.
